calls.message: Build a REST Blog API in Python using only the standard library (http.server + sqlite3). CRUD for posts, X-API-Key auth, JSON bodies, localhost:8080, single file blog_api.py.
calls.result:
I wrote `blog_api.py` in the working directory. I tested it with curl against a throwaway database. Create, patch, put, list, delete and the 404 after delete all worked. A request without a key got 401 earlier in testing. I didn't test oversized bodies or invalid JSON.

Start it with `BLOG_API_KEY=yourkey python3 blog_api.py`. It listens on `127.0.0.1:8080` and stores posts in `blog.db`. Set `BLOG_DB` to use a different file. If you don't set `BLOG_API_KEY`, the key defaults to `dev-key` and the server prints a warning.

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/posts` | Lists posts, newest first. Takes `?limit=` (default 50, max 200) and `?offset=`. |
| POST | `/posts` | Creates a post and returns 201. Needs `title` and `content`; `author` is optional. |
| GET | `/posts/<id>` | Returns one post. |
| PUT | `/posts/<id>` | Replaces the post. `title` and `content` are required; a missing `author` resets to empty. |
| PATCH | `/posts/<id>` | Updates only the fields you send. |
| DELETE | `/posts/<id>` | Deletes the post and returns 204. |

Every request needs an `X-API-Key` header. Bodies and responses are JSON. Errors come back as `{"error": "..."}` with 400, 401, 404, 405, 413, 422 or 500 as appropriate.
